meta.status: DRAFT - must be reviewed by the school's athletic trainer before the demo
meta.disclaimer: ReadyToPlay does not replace a doctor or athletic trainer. Only an athletic trainer or doctor can clear you to play.
meta.estimatePolicy: Every estimate starts at maxDays (the conservative end) and the full range is shown. Improving check-ins can move it toward minDays but never below it. Getting worse never moves it earlier.

emergency.title: Get emergency help now
emergency.message: Call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room. Tell your coach or athletic trainer right away.

see_care_today.title: See the athletic trainer or a doctor today
see_care_today.message: Stop playing. This needs a real check before any recovery plan. We'll show you where to go.

see_trainer.title: Check in with your athletic trainer first
see_trainer.message: This might need a brace, splint, or exam. Your trainer can start your plan once they've looked at it.

plan.title: You can start a recovery plan
plan.message: No warning signs found. Follow the plan, do your daily check-in, and still tell your athletic trainer.

globalRedFlags.question: Did you hit your head, or do you have a headache, dizziness, confusion, or blurry vision?
globalRedFlags.note: Any possible head injury goes to the trainer under the school's concussion protocol. No plan is ever built.

globalRedFlags.question: Do you have chest pain or trouble breathing?
Is the injured area numb, tingling, cold, or does it feel weak?
Does it look bent or out of place, or did you hear or feel a 'pop' when it happened?
Is the pain 8 out of 10 or worse, or did it swell up very fast?

headInjury.message: Head injuries always go to your athletic trainer or a doctor. Do not return to play today. ReadyToPlay never builds a plan for a head injury.
emergencySigns: Acting strange, more confused, restless, or agitated
Passed out, getting more and more sleepy, or can't stay awake
Slurred speech, weakness, numbness, or clumsiness
A headache that gets worse and won't go away
One pupil bigger than the other, or double vision

otherPain.message: We only build plans for ankle, shoulder, hamstring, and wrist injuries. For anything else, answer the warning-sign questions and we'll point you to the right care.

checkInRules.question: Since yesterday, any new numbness or tingling, or a sudden jump in pain or swelling?

checkInRules.rule: Pain score higher than the day before on 2 check-ins in a row

rules.if: pain >= 7 OR any function test failed
pain 4-6 OR any function test 'with difficulty'
pain <= 3 AND all function tests passed

selfTestScoring.swellingRule: Swelling 'A lot' counts the same as a function test answered 'With difficulty'.

rice.rest: Stop the activity that hurt it. Use crutches for a leg injury if walking hurts.
rice.ice: Cold pack wrapped in a towel for 20 minutes, a few times a day. Never put ice right on skin.
rice.compression: Elastic wrap, snug but not tight.
rice.elevation: Keep it raised above your heart when resting.

locations.label: Outside of the ankle
locations.hint: Your foot rolled inward. This is the most common sprain.

locations.label: Above the ankle, front of the lower leg
locations.hint: Your foot got twisted outward, often in a collision. Hurts more when you turn your foot out.
locations.note: High ankle sprains usually take 6-8 weeks or longer, about twice as long as a normal sprain. Get your trainer or a doctor to confirm.

locations.label: Inside of the ankle
locations.note: Inside-ankle sprains are less common and harder to judge at home. A trainer or doctor should check it before you start a plan.

redFlags.question: Can you take 4 steps on it right now? (Limping is OK.)
redFlags.note: Ottawa Ankle Rules: unable to bear weight for 4 steps means it needs an X-ray check.

redFlags.question: Press gently on the back edge and tip of the ankle bones on both sides, the bump on the outside middle of your foot, and the bump on the inside middle of your foot. Does it hurt right on the bone?
redFlags.note: Ottawa Ankle/Foot Rules bony points: lateral/medial malleolus, base of 5th metatarsal, navicular.

selfTests.question: How bad is the pain right now? (0-10)
Can you walk normally across the room?
Can you point your toes up and down and draw circles with your foot?

see_someone.note: Possible grade 3 (complete tear): 6-12 weeks and sometimes surgery. Not planned by the app.

trainerCheckDay.reason: Exams are more accurate 4-7 days after the injury.

protect: Brace or wrap for about 5-10 days
Start gentle range-of-motion in the first week
motion: Ankle alphabet (trace letters with your toes)
return: Wear a lace-up or semi-rigid brace during sports (recommended for up to 12 months)

locations.label: Outer side of the shoulder
locations.hint: Worse when you lift your arm out to the side or overhead.

locations.label: Front of the shoulder
locations.hint: Can spread down the front of your arm.

locations.label: Top of the shoulder
locations.hint: Often after falling on your shoulder or getting hit on it.
locations.note: Pain on top after a fall or hit can be a shoulder separation (AC joint). Mild ones heal in about 2 weeks, worse ones take 6-8 weeks or more, and only an exam can tell which. A bump on top means see care today.

redFlags.question: Did it start suddenly with a snap, and now your arm feels weak?
redFlags.note: Sudden snap plus immediate weakness can mean a rotator cuff tear.

redFlags.question: Can you raise your arm out to the side and over your head?
Does it hurt at night or wake you up?
Do you have a fever, or is the shoulder red and hot?

selfTests.question: How bad is the pain right now? (0-10)
Can you lift your arm straight overhead?
Can you reach behind your back like tucking in a shirt?
Can you do everyday things (backpack, brushing hair) without pain?

moderate.note: More serious cases can take several months. Trainer or doctor sets the timeline.

protect: Rest from throwing and overhead motions
Ice 20 minutes a few times a day
strength: Resistance-band rotator cuff exercises (trainer to confirm)
sport: Warm up with flexibility work first
Gradual return to throwing / overhead sport motions

hamstring.name: Hamstring strain
hamstring.locationQuestion: Where on the back of your thigh does it hurt most?

locations.label: Middle of the back of the thigh
locations.hint: The most common spot for a pulled hamstring.

locations.label: High up, near the buttock
locations.hint: Right where the leg meets the buttock.
locations.note: Pain this high can mean the tendon is injured or pulled off the bone. Tendon injuries can take months and sometimes need surgery.

locations.label: Low, right behind the knee
locations.hint: Just above the back of the knee.
locations.note: Pain close to the knee can mean the tendon pulled off the bone. A doctor should check it.

redFlags.question: Is there a lot of bruising on the back of your leg?
redFlags.note: Heavy bruising can mean the tendon pulled off the bone.

redFlags.question: Can you walk without a big limp?

selfTests.question: How bad is the pain right now? (0-10)
Lying on your stomach, can you bend your knee against light resistance?
Can you gently straighten your leg and lean forward a little?

see_someone.note: Possible grade 3 (complete tear): several months and sometimes surgery.

trainerCheckDay.reason: MedlinePlus advises a follow-up 1-2 weeks after the injury.

strength: Gradual hamstring strengthening (trainer to confirm exercises)
return: Same strength and flexibility as the other leg

wrist.name: Wrist sprain

locations.label: Thumb side
locations.hint: Often after falling on an outstretched hand.
locations.note: We'll do an extra check for a hidden broken bone (scaphoid), which is common on this side.

locations.label: Back or middle of the wrist
locations.hint: The top of your wrist, above the back of your hand.

locations.label: Pinky side
locations.hint: Might click or pop when you turn your wrist.
locations.note: Pinky-side pain can be a cartilage injury (TFCC) that heals slower than a normal sprain. Get it checked before starting a plan.

redFlags.question: Give a thumbs-up. Press in the little hollow at the base of your thumb on the back of your wrist. Does it hurt there?
redFlags.note: Tenderness here can mean a scaphoid fracture, which is often missed and mistaken for a sprain.

redFlags.question: Can you move all your fingers and make a fist?
Does the wrist feel loose, unstable, or like it locks or catches?

selfTests.question: How bad is the pain right now? (0-10)
Can you bend your wrist up and down?
Can you grip a water bottle and twist the cap?

moderate.note: Moderate sprains often need a splint. Trainer or doctor sets the plan.

wrist.noImprovementNote: Pain or swelling that lasts more than 48 hours should be checked, because wrist fractures can hide on early X-rays.

sport: Catching, passing, and weight-bearing drills (push-up position) only when pain-free
